title: The Media Bias Taxonomy: A Systematic Literature Review on the Forms and Automated Detection of Media Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic literature review of automated detection methods, including traditional NLP (lexicons, word counts), transformer-based machine learning (BERT, RoBERTa), non-transformer machine learning (SVM, LSTM), and graph-based approaches to classify political stance, hyperpartisanship, and selective coverage.

Reviewing computational approaches (dense and sparse word embeddings, fine-tuned language models, and sentiment analysis) to detect framing bias, epistemological bias, subjective word choices, spin, and connotation bias in text.

Surveying methods such as Word Embedding Association Tests (WEAT), centering resonance analysis, and neural networks (e.g., bidirectional LSTMs and transformers) to detect stereotypical associations, demographic under-representation, and hate speech.

Evaluating human-centered research methods, user perception studies, annotator background analyses, and recipient-oriented interventions (e.g., browser widgets, inoculation messages) to measure and mitigate phenomena like the Hostile Media Phenomenon, selective exposure, and confirmation bias.
